$comment: This file may name environment variables but must NEVER contain an API key value.
'standard' is the reference workspace: the one you pull from and the one the versioned JSON belongs to.
Push to standard is the identity function; push to hipaa substitutes each 'standard' id for its 'hipaa' one.
'name' is documentation for the reader and is allowed to be non-unique. The lookup key is 'standard'.
Voices are deliberately absent: adding a Voice Library voice to another workspace preserves its voice_id, so voice ids are identity across workspaces and need no mapping.
'deploy_to' says which workspaces an agent ships to. An agent absent from a workspace's list is skipped there with no flag and no conditional, and is not linted against it.

'deploy_order' is the order deploy.yml walks the workspaces, and it is not alphabetical by accident: HIPAA goes first because a failure there leaves production untouched, whereas a standard-first failure would leave HIPAA stale after production had already moved.

The privacy overlay holds only the three fields the API actually honours, verified by creating a throwaway agent and reading it back: zero_retention_mode, record_voice and retention_days. delete_audio and delete_transcript_and_pii are accepted and silently returned as false, so asserting them would fail every deploy forever. retention_days must be -1, not 0 — the API rejects the agent outright otherwise.

'requires' on a test names the mappings whose behaviour it exercises, as "<kind>/<name>". A test is skipped in any workspace whose 'omitted' list covers that dependency: the behaviour was stripped from the config there on purpose, so the test could only ever be red. It is skipped by name and reason in the log, never silently.

ALL IDS IN THIS FILE ARE PLACEHOLDERS. Run the pipeline against your own workspaces after creating the agent, tools and tests there (`agents pull` / `tools pull` / `tests pull` write the real ids back).
